slides.title: When user input runs on your Node server
slides.summary: SSJI is XSS on the server: user data reaches eval or a similar sink and runs with your server's privileges.
body: Node.js powers SSR frameworks, BFFs and build tools. If user input reaches a function that evaluates code, the attacker runs JavaScript on the server: reading files and secrets, or starting processes.

ul: NoSQL queries built from raw request objects ({ "$where": "…" }).

body: <mark>Never evaluate user input as code. There's no safe way to sanitize JavaScript.</mark>

body.note: Node's own docs say the vm module is not a security mechanism. Don't use it to run untrusted code.

blocks.title: calc.js
source: import { evaluate } from 'mathjs'; // a real parser, no eval

figure.alt: A request with ?expr=require("fs").readFileSync(".env") arrives at a Node server whose handler calls eval on the query parameter. The evaluated code runs with the process's permissions, shown as four red boxes: the file system (read source and .env files), environment variables (database passwords and API keys), child_process (run shell commands), and the internal network. The fix: never evaluate input; use a real parser or a lookup table, and run Node with least privilege.

slides.title: Related server-side injections
slides.summary: Prototype pollution, command injection and NoSQL injection follow the same pattern: untrusted data steering code.

ul: Prototype pollution: merging untrusted JSON like {"__proto__": {"isAdmin": true}} into objects changes every object in the process. Use Map, Object.create(null) or schema-validated objects, and keep merge libraries updated.
Command injection: use execFile / spawn with an argument array instead of exec with a string.
NoSQL injection: validate types, so { "$gt": "" } can't arrive where a string was expected.

body: <mark>Validate the shape and type of every request body before it reaches business logic.</mark>

body.note: Run Node with the least privilege it needs. Node's permission model (--permission, stable since Node 23.5) can restrict file system, child process and worker access.
